A dry arid expanse of hard packed earth, its gritty and thin topsoil 
is blown across the flat plains in great storms of dust, feeding 
the eastern Four Moon Lakes. The plant life on the Grayfynn have 
adapted and proved to be hardier than most flora on the island; 
tough rocky exteriors and thorny spines protect deep rooted 
plants that can withstand both the long dry season and the 
voracious herbivores that migrate over these lands. Fortunately 
these same adaptations then provide rich sources of water if one 
knows which spiked plant is ready for harvesting.
Grayfynn
One of the coldest climates outside of the high peaks of the 
Splitspine, this raised plateau of chilled winds and frost laden 
earth leaves little to be desired. Draffers make good use of these 
heights as they are safe to rear their young while descending to 
the northern shores to prey on coastal daugon. When the biting 
wind picks up, bonestalk reeds that grow along the rivers rustle 
with the hollow sounds of winter.

Land Of Wind And Sky
The eastern cliffs that border this land shroud much of the 
morning in shadow, yet these lands grow verdant and fertile still 
as the dust that blows north from the Grayfynn wastes carries 
rich phosphorus to nourish the Duskdown prairies. While gentle 
khanaur graze in the cool air of dawn’s shadow, by evening, 
the golden sunset lights the Stoanhall cliff entrances, allowing 
brilliant growths of ivy to reach deep into the tunnels where 
tormull larvae crawl in their numberless thousands, feasting on 
the wayward life that attempts to colonize their darkened pits.

Clinging to the southern edge of Sol’Kesh, the Meadow Fall provides a stretch of verdant fields, enriched by rivers that bleed out to the 
ocean from the arid Grayfynn above. This sliver of blooming life provides more than just abundant flower fields, but a safe haven for the 
flocks of maedrynn that terrorize the northern wastes above. Fortunately for this idyllic coast, most of the year these hummingbirds 
individually flutter about from flower to flower instead, drinking plant nectar and using the thick colorful foliage to roost. Similarly to 
the Valedayn in the north east, arthropod mega-fauna dominate these lands. Though the sap filled bloomux is not to be found this far 
south, khanaur roam in great numbers along the coast, digging up the salt-blown earth in search of roots, further turning the soil for 
more flowers to take root. These slow moving insects keep a wary eye out for the silver glimmer of drafian silk whenever they near the 
sparse wealdwoods that encroach in from the Shiverrun’s edge, their toxic silk stretching from distant trees to ward off many of the 
Grayfynn’s aggressive predators that often invade during long droughts.
Meadow Fall
A wide vista of wet dunes, waves of sand mirrors the ocean that 
it stretches towards. While the tide can wane and wax over much 
of the landscape, it is the pervasive damp sand from the porous 
bedrock below that gives this location its unique properties. 
Besides some tenacious dune grass, most creatures have difficulty 
sustaining themselves on these sodden sandy plains, yet ocean 
faring birds will congregate in their thousands, nesting in 
safety from the general lack of terrestrial predators. Though this 
sanctuary can be short lived as axilot, migrating from Valedayn, 
rush out during mating season to barrel into nests to quickly 
trample eggs and feast on the spilled yolk. While rare, nicalliath 
are well suited to this environment, their chitin blades clashing 
over beached megafauna.
